entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The Underworld of Hades. The dead are ferried across the river Styx by Charon — and only those buried with a coin may pay his fare.
Drink from the river Lethe and you forget all you ever were. Most shades do.
Hades rules these halls; the gods above only watch. Cross the Styx, wanderer — and do not look back.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The Styx waits, cold and patient. Down into Hades again.

entries.speaker: greece_zeus
lines: So Olympus sends a soul to walk my brother's halls. Bold.
Prove worthy below, and the lightning may yet remember your name.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Beyond the seen world lies niskala — the unseen, where spirits and demons dwell.
Here walks Rangda, queen of the leyak, locked in endless balance with the lion Barong. Neither truly wins; that is the order of things.
Tread with respect, soul. To those who still honor it, this realm is no mere myth.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The gamelan rings in the dark. The unseen stirs again.

entries.speaker: bali_acintya
lines: I am Acintya — the unconceivable, the source and the silence.
Disturb the balance only so far as you must. Then go.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The Duat — the night-road that the sun itself must sail to be reborn each dawn.
Here your heart is weighed against the feather of Ma'at. Heavier with sin, and Ammit the devourer eats it; lighter, and you pass.
Twelve gates, twelve hours of night. Osiris waits at the end of them.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The scales of Ma'at hang ready. Into the night-road once more.

entries.speaker: egypt_osiris
lines: I am Osiris, who died and rose again to judge the dead.
Let your heart be light, traveler — or feed the Devourer.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Helheim, beneath a root of the world-tree. Not the bright hall of slain warriors — this is where the rest are sent.
Those who die of sickness or of age walk the long Helvegr down into the mist, past the hound Garmr.
Hel rules here — half-living, half-corpse, daughter of Loki. Few climb back up the road.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Frost and silence. The Helvegr leads down again.

entries.speaker: norse_odin
lines: I am Odin, who hung nine nights upon the tree to wrest wisdom from death.
Walk Hel's road, then. Learn what I learned.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Yomi-no-kuni, the shadowed land of the dead, where Izanami the mother-goddess went and could not leave.
Izanagi fled her rotting form and sealed the way with a great boulder. Eat the food of Yomi, and you too are bound here.
Touch nothing, taste nothing, soul — and perhaps the road back stays open.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Yomi's gloom presses close. Eat nothing here.

entries.speaker: japan_amaterasu
lines: I am Amaterasu, born of my father's flight from this very dark.
Bring no decay back with you into the light.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Mictlan, nine levels deep, where every soul not claimed by sun or storm must go.
Four years the dead journey down — crossing a wide river on the back of a red dog, past mountains that crush and winds made of knives.
At the bottom wait Mictlantecuhtli and his queen, lord and lady of the dead.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: Nine levels down, the bone-road waits again.

entries.speaker: aztec_mictlantecuhtli
lines: I am Mictlantecuhtli. Every road ends at my throne of bone.
You come early — and still breathing. Curious.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: ...This is not in the Book. No Styx, no Duat, no Helheim. No coin, no feather, no bone-road.
I have guided the dead of a hundred faiths. This place answers to none of them — and I... I do not know the way.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: The map simply... ends. For the first time, the ferryman falls silent.

entries.speaker: greece_zeus
lines: Olympus cannot pierce these clouds. Whatever dreams below is older than my father, and his father before him.
We gods speak to you now because no god rules HERE. Go carefully, little soul.

entries.speaker: egypt_osiris
lines: No feather can weigh what sleeps in this water. Ma'at herself turns her eyes away.
This is not the night-road. This is what the night-road fears.

entries.speaker: norse_odin
lines: Nine nights I hung for wisdom — and even I was never shown THIS drowned city.
Its name does not fit a mortal mouth. R'lyeh. Speak it once, then not again.

entries.speaker: aztec_mictlantecuhtli
lines: Nine levels are mine, and none descend this far. You walk past where death itself stops.
The Old One does not judge, does not ferry, does not weigh. It simply WAKES. Pray it does not.

entries.speaker: japan_amaterasu
lines: My light has crossed every dark — Yomi, the night, the grave. It does not reach HERE.
Whatever lies beneath this sea was old when the first sun was lit. I am... afraid for you.

entries.speaker: bali_acintya
lines: I am the unconceivable — and even I cannot conceive of what dreams below.
We gods do not agree on much. On THIS, we are united: do not wake it. Yet you must.

entries.speaker: hell_cthulhu
lines: You are a candle held to a drowned sun. I dreamed your gods before they were born — and I will dream them after.

entries.speaker: hell_cthulhu
lines: So. The candle still burns. Then I shall WAKE.

entries.speaker: greece_zeus
lines: No— NO! It still MOVES! My thunder turns to ash in my hand — it BURNS me!

entries.speaker: egypt_osiris
lines: The scales shatter! I cannot weigh it — it unmakes me — AAAGH!

entries.speaker: norse_odin
lines: This is no Ragnarok I foresaw. It WAKES. My eye— my eye bleeds light!

entries.speaker: aztec_mictlantecuhtli
lines: Even death recoils! It drinks the dark — it drinks ME — flee!

entries.speaker: japan_amaterasu
lines: My light gutters out! Hero, I cannot shield you — AAAH!

entries.speaker: bali_acintya
lines: The wheel breaks! Such pain — such PAIN — run, little flame, RUN!

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: And every heaven that breathed in relief now SCREAMS as one — the Dreamer was only stirring.

entries.speaker: greece_zeus
lines: It is done! Olympus breathes again — the hero has slain the Dreamer!

entries.speaker: egypt_osiris
lines: Balance is restored. The scales tip back to the living. We thank you.

entries.speaker: norse_odin
lines: Even Ragnarok did not frighten that thing. You felled it. Skål, mortal.

entries.speaker: aztec_mictlantecuhtli
lines: The deep one returns to the dark. The dead may rest. You have our thanks.

entries.speaker: japan_amaterasu
lines: The sun reaches even here now. You have done what gods feared to attempt.

entries.speaker: bali_acintya
lines: The wheel turns clean once more. Be honoured, little flame.

entries.speaker: narrator
lines: For a heartbeat, every god in every heaven exhales as one... too soon.
